methodological_rigor.justification: BESTDR employs a statistically principled continuous-time Markov branching process (CTMBP) framework with multivariate normal likelihood approximation justified by Central Limit Theorem for large populations. Hamiltonian Monte Carlo via Stan is used for Bayesian posterior estimation with credible intervals reported throughout. Validation includes in silico simulations (with known ground truth parameter recovery within 90% credible intervals), orthogonal comparison against lineage-tracing data, and real experimental cisplatin data on HCT116 p53-VKI cells. Hierarchical modeling applied across breast cancer, PC9-derived NSCLC, and SCLC HTS datasets. Comparisons with existing methods (GR metric, Static/Toxic ODE, bdChemo Gaussian process) are quantitative and fair. Statistical methodology is exemplary.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: This is a methodological/statistical framework paper applied to preclinical in vitro data - Oxford LoE 5. Clinical relevance is indirect but meaningful: mechanism-specific drug response quantification (cytostatic vs cytotoxic vs state-transition) can improve preclinical drug discovery, biomarker identification, and target prioritization. Directly informs drug development pipelines but does not itself change clinical practice.

reporting_quality.justification: Methods are detailed with specific software versions (Stan v2.34.1, cmdstanr v0.7.1, R v4.3.2, tidyverse v2.0.0, estipop v0.0.1) and public datasets (HTS001, HTS031 from Thunor) with references. Cell line experimental protocols specify drug concentrations, imaging intervals (every 4 hours), and segmentation parameters. The R package is freely available on GitHub with vignettes in Supplementary Appendix. No disease-specific reporting standard applies (methodological); CONSORT/STROBE/etc. do not apply. Authors note cell lines were not authenticated or Mycoplasma-tested which is a limitation acknowledged.

novelty_literature.justification: BESTDR is a genuinely novel statistical framework that links concentration-response curves directly to mechanistic cell-state transition rates (birth, death, state switching) using CTMBP with Bayesian inference. It addresses a real gap in drug discovery methodology by leveraging variance in cell count data (previously treated as noise) to distinguish otherwise-identical net growth scenarios. The hierarchical extension for HTS and flexibility to incorporate multiple CR functional forms (logistic, Gaussian process, splines, neural networks) is methodologically rich. Prior art (DrFIT, GR metrics, bdChemo) is clearly identified and BESTDR extends/complements these.

writing_presentation.justification: Manuscript is exceptionally clear for a statistical methods paper, balancing mathematical rigor (branching process theory, CTMBP likelihood) with accessible narrative (Fig 1 schematic A-H walking through the framework). Abstract is duplicated (formatting artifact). Results are organized logically from simulation validation -> single-drug experimental validation -> multi-cell-line hierarchical extension -> multi-state applications (cell cycle, reprogramming). Comparisons with existing methods are explicit and transparent.

key_strengths: Principled statistical framework using continuous-time Markov branching processes with Bayesian Hamiltonian Monte Carlo inference, exceeding prior dose-response methods in mechanism-specificity
Validated with in silico simulations (recovering ground truth within 90% credible intervals), orthogonal lineage-tracing comparison, and experimental cisplatin HCT116 data
Hierarchical extension to HTS demonstrated across three independent datasets (breast cancer, PC9-NSCLC, SCLC) supporting scalability
Open-source R package with vignettes on GitHub; well-documented software and reproducibility infrastructure
Honest comparison with existing methods (GR metrics, Static/Toxic ODE, bdChemo) including quantitative area-between-curves benchmarks
Handles dead cell clearance issue where ODE methods become unidentifiable, providing important practical advantage
key_concerns: Duplicated abstract indicates manuscript conversion/formatting issue
Cell lines used in bench experiments were not Mycoplasma-tested or authenticated (acknowledged limitation)
Clinical impact is indirect; no patient outcome or biomarker validation
The four-parameter logistic CR function assumption may not always be appropriate (addressed with flexible alternatives but adds modeling complexity)
Computational cost of Hamiltonian Monte Carlo at HTS scale not fully benchmarked against simpler methods
chief_reviewer.rationale: Methodologically novel and statistically exemplary Bayesian framework for mechanism-specific drug response quantification with comprehensive validation and open software release, fitting Tier 2 (JCO Precision Oncology / Cancer Research computational methods-tier) with minor revisions.
